literal: In that fifth month Spark-Delusion entered the Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: That May Mars entered the Southern Dipper.

literal: The prognostication states: "The minister of state dies; troops rise on a great scale."
idiomatic: The omen promised a chief minister’s death and major war.

literal: The Dipper is also the field division of Wu.
idiomatic: The Dipper also marks Wu’s celestial territory.

literal: At this time Prince Zhao of Zhao, Lun, was minister; the next year he usurped the throne; the three princes raised armies and executed him.
idiomatic: Sima Lun was then chief minister; the following year he seized the throne, only for the three princes’ coalition to crush him.

literal: In the second year of Taian, Shi Bing destroyed Yangzhou.
idiomatic: In Taian 2 (303) Shi Bing overran Yangzhou.

literal: In that eighth month Spark-Delusion entered the Winnowing Basket.
idiomatic: That August Mars crossed the Winnowing Basket.

literal: The prognostication states: "The lord of men loses his position; troops rise."
idiomatic: It foretold dethronement and rebellion.

literal: The next year Prince Zhao of Zhao, Lun, usurped the throne and changed the era name.
idiomatic: The next year Sima Lun usurped the throne and proclaimed a new era.

literal: In the second year, second month, the Great White emerged in the west and retrograded into the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In the second month of Yongning 2 Venus rose in the west and backed into the Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication states: "The state loses good government; great ministers make rebellion."
idiomatic: Misrule and ministerial revolt were again portended.

literal: At this time Prince of Qi, Jiong, raised troops to punish Prince Zhao of Zhao, Lun; Lun was destroyed; Jiong held troops and did not attend court, monopolized power and indulged in extravagance; the next year he was put to death.
idiomatic: Prince Sima Jiong of Qi marched against Sima Lun, destroyed him, then quartered his army in the capital, grew insolent and overbearing, and was executed the following year.

literal: In the first year of Yongning, from the first month through the intercalary month, the five planets in turn crossed the sky, moving erratically without pattern.
idiomatic: From New Year through the leap month of Yongning 1 (301) all five planets in turn transited in broad daylight, weaving unpredictably across the zenith.

literal: The *Star Treatise* states: "The sun is yang, the way of the ruler;
idiomatic: The *Star Canon* explains: the sun embodies yang—the ruler’s path;

literal: stars are yin, the way of ministers."
idiomatic: stars embody yin—the ministers’ path."

literal: When the sun comes out then the stars perish; ministers may not monopolize power."
idiomatic: when the sun rises the stars vanish, for subjects must not eclipse their sovereign."

literal: When stars are seen at noon they are called crossing the sky; their prognostication is unfilial ministers and change of king."
idiomatic: Stars visible at noon count as "crossing the sky," portending treason and dynastic turnover."

literal: Now the five planets all crossed the sky—an astral anomaly never before recorded."
idiomatic: Never had all five planets crossed the meridian by day—an omen without precedent in the annals."

literal: Shi’s explanation states: "When the Chronograph Star is seen in daytime, that state will not perish then there is great chaos."
idiomatic: Shi Shen’s school warns that Mercury by day means either ruin or utter turmoil.

literal: After this, terrace ministers and regional shepherds in turn seized great power; the two emperors went into exile; thereupon the six barbarians in succession became kings, each in turn occupying Huaxia—also something never recorded in the canons."
idiomatic: Terrace secretaries and provincial governors then wrested real authority; two emperors fled the capital; steppe peoples took turns enthroning themselves across the North—another novelty unlisted in older star lore."

literal: In that fourth month the Year Star was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: That April Jupiter shone in daylight.

literal: In the fifth month the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: In May Venus appeared by day.

literal: The prognostication is the same as before.
idiomatic: The same omen readings applied as earlier.

literal: In the seventh month the Year Star guarded Emptiness and Rooftop.
idiomatic: In July Jupiter stationed between Emptiness and Rooftop.

literal: The prognostication states: "When wood guards Emptiness and Rooftop, there is military anxiety."
idiomatic: Jupiter lingering there augurs war and worry.

literal: Emptiness and Rooftop are the field division of Qi.
idiomatic: That sector maps onto the old Qi heartland.

literal: One reading says: "Guarding Emptiness means famine;
idiomatic: One gloss adds: a long stay over Emptiness promises famine;

literal: guarding Rooftop means corvée labor is excessive and the lower folk are exhausted."
idiomatic: over Rooftop it means crushing levies and a drained populace."

literal: The Chronograph Star entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure; the prognostication states "there is internal disorder," one reading says "the host of ministers kill one another."
idiomatic: Mercury in the Supreme Palace Enclosure reads as palace turmoil—or ministers turning blades on one another."

literal: The Great White guarded the right Ye Gate; the prognostication states: "There will be troops, there will be chaos, there will be bandits."
idiomatic: Venus guarding the right palace gate foretells arms, riot, and brigandage."

literal: In the eighth month, on wuwu, the Filling Star transgressed the Left Enforcer, and again transgressed the Upper Minister; the prognostication states "the upper minister has anxiety."
idiomatic: On wuwu in August Saturn struck the Left Enforcer and the Upper Minister stars—ill omens for the senior minister."

literal: Spark-Delusion guarded Net; the prognostication states "Zhao and Wei have disaster."
idiomatic: Mars stationed in the Net sector boded disaster for Zhao and Wei.

literal: The Chronograph Star guarded the Coach-and-Ghosts; the prognostication states "Qin has disaster."
idiomatic: Mercury lingering on the Ghosts predicted calamity in the old Qin region.
